subject: Supplier control artefacts and hosting locations
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@medigen.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Angela Park <angela.park@medigen.com>, compliance@medigen.com
Date: 2026-05-09T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Request: inventory of hosting locations & supplier artefacts for upcoming SOC 2

Hi Laura,

We’re kicking off our SOC 2 readiness work and need a compact bundle from Redwood that lists where customer data may be processed and which suppliers (subprocessors) you use for hosting, logging, telemetry, and KMS. Specifically could you provide: 

- A roster of subprocessors (name, service, country of residency, whether they have access to plaintext customer data)
- Hosting/region map for the services that process customer content (hosted API, dedicated pools, private options)
- Any artifact(s) that assert KMS ownership or residency (short statement/PDF is fine)
- A short CAIQ mapping or pointer to controls that cover data residency and key management

We need the package for our auditor by next Wednesday (2026-05-13). If you have a single bundle/link for auditors that’s ideal.

Thanks — we can jump on a quick call if needed.

Sanjay Rao
Senior IT Compliance Manager
Medigen Health

---
Attachment: auditor_questionnaire_template.xlsx (xls, 180KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@medigen.com>
Cc: Angela Park <angela.park@medigen.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: inventory of hosting locations & supplier artefacts for upcoming SOC 2

Hi Sanjay,

Thanks for the note — we can get you a compact bundle by EOD Monday (2026-05-11). I’ve started a shared folder for the auditor and attached the high-level roster and hosting CSV here for quick review. Key points up-front:

- We maintain a living subprocessor roster (attached) that includes residency and access column flags.
- Hosting locations: hosted API runs in US and EU cloud regions. Dedicated pools can be pinned to customer-preferred regions; our Private deployment customers host in-customer VPCs/on-prem. See attached CSV.
- KMS: Redwood controls master keys for hosted and dedicated; for Private installs we provide KMS-integration guidance and a signed declaration for key ownership (attached PDF for your auditor).

I’m copying Karthik and Irene to confirm a short CAIQ mapping and to confirm whether any current subprocessors have APAC residency that might affect Medigen’s scoping.

Next steps: please review what’s attached and tell us if the auditor needs additional depth (e.g., full CAIQ evidence bundle vs. a controls mapping). We can also provide a limited privileged-access log extract under NDA if requested.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Trust & Compliance (acting)
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: redwood-subprocessor-roster-2026-05.xlsx (xlsx, 95KB); hosting-locations-2026.csv (csv, 12KB); kms-ownership-declaration-2026.pdf (pdf, 28KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: inventory of hosting locations & supplier artefacts for upcoming SOC 2

Team — forwarding Medigen’s request (below). I sent them the high-level roster and hosting map, but they’ll likely ask for a short CAIQ controls mapping and confirmation on any APAC-resident subprocessors. Can you each own the following by EOD Monday (2026-05-11)?

Karthik: please review the attached roster and confirm the residency flags and the 'access to plaintext' column. If any subprocessor is APAC-resident, note if processing is limited to metadata only or includes content. If you find gaps, flag them and prepare wording we can share with the auditor.

Irene: produce a two-page CAIQ compact that maps our controls for Data Residency, Key Management, and Access Controls. The auditor prefers a concise mapping rather than the full CAIQ matrix — include references to where full evidence lives (drive links).

Also: if either of you think we should include a short statement about our fallback routing (model variant fallbacks) for resiliency, mention it; the auditor may be validating continuity as part of system inventory.

Thanks — please reply-all with the final artifacts so I can forward one consolidated bundle.

Laura

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-05-11T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: inventory of hosting locations & supplier artefacts for upcoming SOC 2

Hi Sanjay — Laura, Irene (cc)

Thanks for the patience; attaching a consolidated bundle for your auditor. Highlights below for quick consumption:

1) Subprocessor roster (attached workbook) — includes: provider name, service category (hosting, telemetry, logging, KMS, CI/CD), country of primary provisioning, whether vendor has access to customer plaintext, and minimal contract residency notes. Current status: no primary hosting subprocessors in APAC for our hosted API offering; we do have telemetry/observability partners whose processing is region-agnostic (they do not store customer content in plaintext).

2) Hosting locations (hosting-locations-2026.csv) — lists service endpoints and default regions. Hosted API: US (us-west2, us-central1) and EU (europe-west1). Dedicated pools: configured per-customer and can be requested in specific cloud regions. Private: customer-managed.

3) KMS statement (kms-ownership-declaration-2026.pdf) — confirms Redwood retains control of master keys for hosted and dedicated modes; for Private deployments we provide a standard KMS integration guide.

4) CAIQ mapping (caiq-mapping-compact-2026.pdf) — Irene prepared a two-page mapping that points auditors to the full evidence drive folder and lists control owners.

Attachments included in the shared folder: redwood-subprocessor-roster-2026-05.xlsx, hosting-locations-2026.csv, kms-ownership-declaration-2026.pdf, caiq-mapping-compact-2026.pdf

If your auditor needs a short privileged-access log extract or a signed statement on data processing pathways, say the word and we’ll scope that under the appropriate NDA.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference
